title: NSG Flow Log Analysis

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.4 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.4 search returns zero rows.

description: NSG Flow Logs provide Azure network-level visibility. Detects blocked traffic, anomalous patterns, and lateral movement within VNets.
value: Detecting nsg flow log analysis early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable NSG Flow Logs (Version 2) on all NSGs. Send to a storage account. Ingest via Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices. Create dashboards for denied traffic and top talkers.

knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:nsgflowlog`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable NSG Flow Logs (Version 2) on all NSGs. Send to a storage account. Ingest via Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices. Create dashboards for denied traffic and top talkers.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:nsgflowlog" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:nsgflowlog" flowState="D"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.4_nsg_flow_log_analysis_4"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:nsgflowlog` in `index=azure` to detect nsg flow log analysis. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_4_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (top denied flows), Sankey diagram, Timechart, Map..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of nsg flow log analysis so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
